n: Orson Pratt, Parley’s nineteen-year-old brother, was baptized on his birthday in September 1830 and came to Fayette to learn his duty. Christ addresses him tenderly as “my son.”

f.g: Orson Pratt later became an apostle and a noted scientist and scriptural scholar.

n: Christ is the light and life of the world, shining in a darkness that doesn’t comprehend it.

f.w: a light which shineth in darkness

n: Christ loved the world enough to give his life so believers could become God’s children — which is why Orson is called “my son.”

f.w: so loved the world that he gave his own life
blessed are you because you have believed

n: He is even more blessed to be called to preach.
Orson is to cry repentance loudly and long, preparing the way for the Second Coming.

f.w: preparing the way of the Lord for his second coming

n: Christ will soon come in a cloud with power and great glory.

f.w: come in a cloud with power and great glory

n: His coming will be a great day; every nation will tremble.
Before it, signs will appear in sun, moon, and stars, and destruction awaits the wicked.

f.w: the stars shall refuse their shining

n: Orson should speak boldly and prophesy by the Holy Ghost.

f.w: prophesy, and it shall be given by the power of the Holy Ghost

n: If faithful, the Lord is with him until he comes.
Christ is coming quickly; he is Orson’s Lord and Redeemer.
